Command: Do Not Move Your Neighbour's Landmark
Summary: Thou shalt not remove thy neighbour's landmark, which they of old time have set in thine inheritance. This is the boundary-stone law, distinct from the live Inheritance row, whose Numbers and Deuteronomy 21 ranges do not include Deuteronomy 19:14.
Commandment: Do not remove your neighbour's ancient landmark in the inheritance God has given.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as civil. Boundaries are property made visible: moving one is theft that no one can see at once, because the field itself looks unchanged. The New Testament does not restate boundary stones, but it does restate the theft they guard against (Ephesians 4:28).
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: the landmark is the inherited boundary set by former generations, and moving it steals land by stealth. Scripture states the prohibition without a separate reason (Deuteronomy 19:14).
